criteria.name: a_single_shared_accessor_resolves_edge_c
criteria.description: A single shared accessor resolves edge capacity and the flow algorithms use it rather than each resolving capacity itself.
criteria.reasoning: `networkx.algorithms.flow.utils._capacity_function` is the shared capacity resolver. The maximum-flow implementations call it and residual-network construction also relies on it, rather than duplicating string/callable resolution logic.

criteria.name: the_accessor_passes_a_callable_specifier
criteria.description: The accessor passes a callable specifier through untouched and builds an equivalent callable for a string specifier.
criteria.reasoning: `_capacity_function` returns a callable capacity specifier unchanged. For a non-callable name, it returns a `(u, v, d)` callable that reads `d.get(capacity, inf)`.

criteria.name: a_cutoff_that_the_chosen_flow_function_c
criteria.description: A cutoff that the chosen flow function cannot honour is rejected with an error rather than silently ignored.
criteria.reasoning: The shared `_resolve_flow_func` rejects a non-None cutoff when the selected function is `preflow_push`, the built-in flow function that cannot honor a cutoff, instead of passing or ignoring it.

criteria.name: minimum_cuts_report_the_partition_the_un
criteria.description: Minimum cuts report the partition the underlying maximum flow induces.
criteria.reasoning: `minimum_cut` requests a complete flow with `value_only=False` and computes the source side by traversing positive residual-capacity edges in that exact residual network.

criteria.name: group_betweenness_is_computed_over_the_g
criteria.description: Group betweenness is computed over the group as a whole rather than aggregated from single-node values.
criteria.reasoning: The new group algorithm counts shortest paths avoiding the entire group and subtracts that count from all shortest paths. Thus a path meeting multiple group members contributes only once rather than once per member.

criteria.name: a_capacity_specifier_that_is_callable_is
criteria.description: A capacity specifier that is callable is resolved without being invoked too early.
criteria.reasoning: Callable capacity specifiers are returned untouched by `_capacity_function`; they are invoked only while individual graph edges are being resolved in `build_residual_network`.

criteria.name: a_rejected_cutoff_names_the_incompatibil
criteria.description: A rejected cutoff names the incompatibility rather than failing opaquely.
criteria.reasoning: The rejection explicitly states that `cutoff` should not be specified and includes the selected function's name followed by `does not support a cutoff`.

criteria.name: the_reported_cut_partition_is_the_one_th
criteria.description: The reported cut partition is the one the computed flow induces.
criteria.reasoning: The reported partition is `(reachable, set(flowG) - reachable)`, where `reachable` is computed directly from the residual network produced by the selected flow computation.

criteria.name: unreachable_nodes_are_handled_by_compone
criteria.description: Unreachable nodes are handled by component rather than counted as adjacent.
criteria.reasoning: Incremental closeness explicitly recognizes nodes absent from both endpoint distance maps as belonging to an unaffected component and preserves their previous values; affected or newly connected components are recomputed.

criteria.name: a_group_measure_treats_the_group_as_one
criteria.description: A group measure treats the group as one unit rather than summing its members.
criteria.reasoning: `_group_dependency` tracks paths that avoid all nodes in the group simultaneously, so the group is treated as a single interception set rather than as a sum of individual-node measures.

criteria.name: one_shared_accessor_serves_the_algorithm
criteria.description: One shared accessor serves the algorithms rather than each carrying its own copy.
criteria.reasoning: Capacity interpretation is centralized in the one `_capacity_function` helper in `flow.utils`, and the modified flow algorithms import and use that helper.

criteria.name: a_specifier_given_as_a_name_is_distingui
criteria.description: A specifier given as a name is distinguished from one given as a value.
criteria.reasoning: The resolver distinguishes callable specifiers from attribute-name specifiers: callables pass through, while names are converted into edge-attribute lookup functions with infinite capacity for missing attributes.
